newsitem.title: USA: American Home Q1 drug sales grow to $2.1 bln.
newsitem.headline: American Home Q1 drug sales grow to $2.1 bln.

text.p: American Home Products said Tuesday that sales in its pharmaceutical units increased seven percent to $2.1 billion in the first quarter ended march 31, with strong help from U.S. sales Redux and Naprelan (both products were introduced in the 1996 second quarter) and higher sales of Lodine, Ziac, Oruvail, Premarin products and recombinant Factor VIII.
Sales of oral contraceptives and other cardiovascular and pharmaceutical products, and international pharmaceutical sales fell, however.

Consumer health care sales, said the company, rose four percent, period to period, to $495.5 million. The company said while U.S. consumer health care sales increased only two percent, international consumer health care sales increased 11 percent due primarily to higher sales of Centrum, Advil and cough/cold products.

Agricultural product sales rose eight percent, period to period, to $685.7 million, said the company. Domestic sales were up primarily to sales of Steel herbicide and higher sales of Prowl, Status and Assert herbicides. International sales were boosted by higher sales of Pursuit and Scepter herbicides and Acrobat fungicide offset, in part, by lower sales of Caramba fungicide and a 5% unfavorable foreign exchange effect.
